"""Command-line entry points; errors do not print raw event payloads or credentials."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
from pathlib import Path

from aegislake.pipeline import run
from aegislake.review import record_review
from aegislake.synthetic import generate


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="aegislake")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    demo = commands.add_parser("demo", help="Generate synthetic data and run the benchmark")
    demo.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    demo.add_argument("--days", type=int, default=30)
    demo.add_argument("--users", type=int, default=50)
    demo.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    benchmark = commands.add_parser("run", help="Evaluate canonical labeled JSONL")
    benchmark.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True)
    benchmark.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    for command in (demo, benchmark):
        command.add_argument("--train-days", type=int, default=18)
        command.add_argument("--validation-days", type=int, default=6)
        command.add_argument("--capacity", type=int, default=25)
    review = commands.add_parser("review", help="Record a human review locally")
    review.add_argument("--run", type=Path, required=True)
    review.add_argument("--alert-id", required=True)
    review.add_argument("--decision", choices=["true_positive", "false_positive", "needs_context"], required=True)
    review.add_argument("--reviewer", required=True)
    review.add_argument("--note", default="")
    adapter = commands.add_parser("adapt-entra", help="Pseudonymize a local Graph JSON export")
    adapter.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True)
    adapter.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    scoring = commands.add_parser("score", help="Score a future unlabeled batch using an existing run")
    scoring.add_argument("--reference", type=Path, required=True)
    scoring.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True)
    scoring.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    scoring.add_argument("--allow-domain-shift", action="store_true")
    cloud = commands.add_parser("publish", help="Upload only synthetic reports to private Azure storage")
    cloud.add_argument("--run", type=Path, required=True)
    cloud.add_argument("--account", required=True)
    cloud.add_argument("--container", default="reports")
    web = commands.add_parser("serve", help="Explore completed batches in a local interactive dashboard")
    web.add_argument("--runs", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    web.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8767)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command in {"demo", "run"}:
        if args.command == "demo":
            source = args.output / "inputs" / f"demo-{args.days}-{args.users}-{args.seed}.jsonl"
            generate(source, days=args.days, users=args.users, seed=args.seed)
        else:
            source = args.input
        destination = run(source, args.output, train_days=args.train_days, validation_days=args.validation_days,
                          capacity=args.capacity, seed=getattr(args, "seed", 42), synthetic=args.command == "demo")
        print(destination.resolve())
    elif args.command == "review":
        record_review(args.run, args.alert_id, args.decision, args.reviewer, args.note)
        print("Review recorded locally")
    elif args.command == "adapt-entra":
        from aegislake.adapters import adapt_entra

        secret = os.environ.get("AEGIS_PSEUDONYM_KEY", "").encode()
        if len(secret) < 32:
            parser.error("set AEGIS_PSEUDONYM_KEY to a private key of at least 32 bytes")
        print(f"Adapted {adapt_entra(args.input, args.output, secret)} events")
    elif args.command == "score":
        from aegislake.scoring import score

        print(score(args.reference, args.input, args.output, allow_domain_shift=args.allow_domain_shift).resolve())
    elif args.command == "publish":
        from aegislake.azure import publish

        print(f"Published {len(publish(args.run, args.account, args.container))} private synthetic report objects")
    elif args.command == "serve":
        from aegislake.dashboard_server import serve

        serve(args.runs, args.port)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Unlabeled batch scoring from an integrity-checked reference; no pickle loading."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.metadata
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from aegislake import __version__
from aegislake.evaluation import queue_mask
from aegislake.features import build_features
from aegislake.lake import file_sha256, ingest, write_json
from aegislake.models import Models, explain
from aegislake.review import alert_id


def verify_run(run_dir: Path) -> dict:
    manifest = json.loads((run_dir / "manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if manifest["config"]["version"] != __version__:
        raise ValueError("reference code version differs")
    for relative, digest in manifest["artifacts"].items():
        path = (run_dir / relative).resolve()
        if not path.is_relative_to(run_dir.resolve()) or path.is_symlink():
            raise ValueError("invalid manifest path")
        if file_sha256(path) != digest:
            raise ValueError("reference integrity check failed")
    return manifest


def score(reference: Path, source: Path, destination: Path, *, allow_domain_shift: bool = False) -> Path:
    manifest = verify_run(reference)
    for package, expected in manifest["packages"].items():
        if importlib.metadata.version(package) != expected:
            raise ValueError("reference dependency versions differ; reproduce its environment first")
    report = json.loads((reference / "report.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if manifest["config"]["synthetic"] and not allow_domain_shift:
        raise ValueError("synthetic-trained reference requires explicit --allow-domain-shift for new data")
    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    events, quality = ingest(source, destination)
    test = pd.read_parquet(reference / "gold" / "test_features.parquet")
    if events["timestamp"].min() < test["window_end"].max():
        raise ValueError("new scoring data must start after the reference test period ends")
    train = pd.read_parquet(reference / "gold" / "train_features.parquet")
    train_end = pd.Timestamp(report["split_boundaries"]["train_last_window_end"])
    history = pd.read_parquet(reference / "silver")
    history = history.loc[history["timestamp"] < train_end]
    features = build_features(pd.concat([history, events], ignore_index=True), train_end)
    features = features.loc[features["window_start"] >= events["timestamp"].min().floor("15min")].copy()
    models = Models.fit(train, manifest["config"]["seed"])
    champion = report["champion"]
    scores = models.score(features)[champion]
    threshold = report["validation"][champion]["threshold"]
    selected = queue_mask(features, scores, threshold, report["capacity"])
    alerts = []
    for pos, (_, row) in enumerate(features.iterrows()):
        if selected[pos]:
            user, stamp = str(row["user"]), row["window_start"].isoformat()
            alerts.append({
                "alert_id": alert_id(user, stamp), "user": user, "window_start": stamp,
                "window_end": row["window_end"].isoformat(),
                "score": float(scores[pos]), "model": champion, **explain(row),
            })
    (destination / "gold").mkdir()
    features.to_parquet(destination / "gold" / "scored_features.parquet", index=False)
    write_json(destination / "gold" / "alerts.json", alerts)
    from aegislake.report import render_report

    scoring_report = {
        "run_id": "score-" + hashlib.sha256((manifest["run_id"] + file_sha256(source)).encode()).hexdigest()[:20],
        "champion": champion,
        "capacity": report["capacity"], "test": {}, "quality": quality,
        "config": {"synthetic": False},
        "data_notice": ("UNLABELED SCORING BATCH. Effectiveness is unmeasured. "
                        + ("Synthetic-trained reference; domain shift was explicitly allowed."
                           if manifest["config"]["synthetic"] else "Reference collection scope requires review.")),
        "split_boundaries": {"test_first_window": features["window_start"].min().isoformat(),
                             "test_last_window_end": features["window_end"].max().isoformat()},
    }
    render_report(destination, scoring_report, alerts, kind="scoring")
    # The local explorer discovers scoring batches only after this completion marker exists.
    write_json(destination / "scoring.json", {
        "reference_run_id": manifest["run_id"], "input_sha256": file_sha256(source),
        "alerts": len(alerts), "windows": len(features), "quality": quality,
        "warning": "Experimental offline scoring. Domain shift requires separate validation.",
        "metrics": None, "synthetic_reference": manifest["config"]["synthetic"],
        "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    })
    return destination

"""Private synthetic-report publication with Entra authentication and no shared keys."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

from aegislake.scoring import verify_run

PUBLISH_FILES = ("report.html", "mitre.html", "dashboard.html", "dashboard.json", "report.json", "quality.json", "gold/alerts.json",
                 "attack-mapping.json", "dettect-techniques.yaml")


def publish(run_dir: Path, account: str, container: str = "reports") -> list[str]:
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9]{3,24}", account):
        raise ValueError("invalid Azure storage account name")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,61}[a-z0-9]", container) or "--" in container:
        raise ValueError("invalid Azure container name")
    manifest = verify_run(run_dir)
    if manifest["config"].get("synthetic") is not True:
        raise ValueError("only synthetic demonstration reports may be published by this command")
    # Lazy imports leave the local demo independent of Azure packages and credentials.
    from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
    from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient, ContentSettings

    credential = DefaultAzureCredential(exclude_interactive_browser_credential=True)
    uploaded = []
    try:
        with BlobServiceClient(f"https://{account}.blob.core.windows.net", credential=credential) as client:
            for relative in PUBLISH_FILES:
                path = run_dir / relative
                blob = f"{manifest['run_id']}/{relative}"
                mime = {".html": "text/html", ".yaml": "application/yaml"}.get(path.suffix, "application/json")
                with path.open("rb") as handle:
                    client.get_blob_client(container, blob).upload_blob(
                        handle, overwrite=True, content_settings=ContentSettings(content_type=mime)
                    )
                uploaded.append(blob)
            # Manifest is the commit marker, published only after all report uploads succeed.
            client.get_blob_client(container, f"{manifest['run_id']}/publication.json").upload_blob(
                json.dumps({"run_id": manifest["run_id"], "files": uploaded}),
                overwrite=True, content_settings=ContentSettings(content_type="application/json"),
            )
    finally:
        credential.close()
    return uploaded

import json

import pandas as pd
import pytest

from aegislake.azure import publish
from aegislake.pipeline import run
from aegislake.scoring import score, verify_run


def test_end_to_end_manifest_splits_and_idempotency(completed_run):
    source, path = completed_run
    manifest = verify_run(path)
    assert {"mitre.html", "dashboard.html", "dashboard.json", "attack-mapping.json",
            "dettect-techniques.yaml"} <= manifest["artifacts"].keys()
    report = json.loads((path / "report.json").read_text())
    assert report["quality"]["duplicates"] == 1
    assert report["quality"]["rejected"] == 1
    assert "SYNTHETIC" in report["data_notice"]
    train = pd.read_parquet(path / "gold/train_features.parquet")
    validation = pd.read_parquet(path / "gold/validation_features.parquet")
    test = pd.read_parquet(path / "gold/test_features.parquet")
    assert train["window_end"].max() <= validation["window_start"].min()
    assert validation["window_end"].max() <= test["window_start"].min()
    for result in report["test"].values():
        assert result["daily_alerts_max"] <= 12
    assert run(source, path.parent, **{key: manifest["config"][key] for key in
               ("train_days", "validation_days", "capacity", "seed", "synthetic")}) == path


def test_tampered_artifact_is_rejected(completed_run, tmp_path):
    import shutil

    _, path = completed_run
    copy = tmp_path / "copy"
    shutil.copytree(path, copy)
    (copy / "quality.json").write_text("{}")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="integrity"):
        verify_run(copy)


def test_cloud_destination_and_real_data_publication_guard(completed_run, tmp_path):
    import shutil

    _, path = completed_run
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="account"):
        publish(path, "https://evil.example")
    copy = tmp_path / "real"
    shutil.copytree(path, copy)
    manifest = json.loads((copy / "manifest.json").read_text())
    manifest["config"]["synthetic"] = False
    (copy / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="only synthetic"):
        publish(copy, "aegisexample")


def test_unlabeled_future_scoring_has_no_evaluation_metrics(completed_run, event, tmp_path):
    _, reference = completed_run
    source = tmp_path / "future.jsonl"
    source.write_text(json.dumps(event | {
        "timestamp": "2026-02-10T10:01:00Z", "label": None,
    }) + "\n")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="domain-shift"):
        score(reference, source, tmp_path / "refused")
    destination = score(reference, source, tmp_path / "scored", allow_domain_shift=True)
    result = json.loads((destination / "scoring.json").read_text())
    assert result["windows"] == 1
    assert result["metrics"] is None
    dashboard = json.loads((destination / "dashboard.json").read_text())
    assert dashboard["run"]["data_kind"] == "unlabeled"
    assert dashboard["run"]["benchmark"] is None
    assert (destination / "dashboard.html").is_file()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("fail_yaml", [False, True])
def test_cloud_publication_keeps_linked_exports_and_commits_last(completed_run, monkeypatch, fail_yaml):
    import sys
    from types import ModuleType, SimpleNamespace

    from aegislake.azure import PUBLISH_FILES

    _, path = completed_run
    uploads = []
    closed = []

    class Credential:
        def close(self):
            closed.append(True)

    class Blob:
        def __init__(self, name):
            self.name = name

        def upload_blob(self, payload, *, overwrite, content_settings):
            if fail_yaml and self.name.endswith(".yaml"):
                raise RuntimeError("simulated upload failure")
            data = payload.read() if hasattr(payload, "read") else payload
            uploads.append((self.name, data, content_settings.content_type))

    class Client:
        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
            pass

        def __enter__(self):
            return self

        def __exit__(self, *args):
            pass

        def get_blob_client(self, container, name):
            return Blob(name)

    # Exercise the SDK protocol without requiring optional cloud packages or credentials locally.
    modules = {name: ModuleType(name) for name in ("azure", "azure.identity", "azure.storage", "azure.storage.blob")}
    modules["azure.identity"].DefaultAzureCredential = lambda **kwargs: Credential()
    modules["azure.storage.blob"].BlobServiceClient = Client
    modules["azure.storage.blob"].ContentSettings = lambda **kwargs: SimpleNamespace(**kwargs)
    for name, module in modules.items():
        monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, name, module)
    if fail_yaml:
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="simulated"):
            publish(path, "aegisexample")
        assert not any(name.endswith("publication.json") for name, _, _ in uploads)
    else:
        published = publish(path, "aegisexample")
        assert len(published) == len(PUBLISH_FILES)
        assert uploads[-1][0].endswith("publication.json")
        assert json.loads(uploads[-1][1])["files"] == published
        assert any(name.endswith("mitre.html") and mime == "text/html" for name, _, mime in uploads)
        assert any(name.endswith("dettect-techniques.yaml") and mime == "application/yaml"
                   for name, _, mime in uploads)
        assert any(name.endswith("attack-mapping.json") and mime == "application/json"
                   for name, _, mime in uploads)
    assert closed == [True]

README.md:
# AegisLake

> Interactive dashboard release 0.2.0: 61 tests pass locally with 90% measured Python coverage.
> GitHub Actions validation for this release is pending publication; previous release evidence is recorded separately.

## Interactive SOC dashboards

The web interface now includes a native dashboard with linked activity charts, ATT&CK distribution,
a UTC weekday/hour heatmap, top identities and score distributions. Selecting a chart filters every
KPI and the investigation queue. It reads actual AegisLake run outputs, with explicit synthetic,
labeled-evaluation or unlabeled-scoring provenance.

```bash
aegislake demo --seed 7 --output runs
aegislake serve --runs runs --port 8767
# Open http://127.0.0.1:8767/dashboard.html
```

The local read-only API discovers completed batches without restarting. Optional 30-second polling
can follow the latest batch, while manual refresh preserves filters for the current batch. Scoring
batches get their own dashboard without inherited precision/recall. Each run also includes a
self-contained `dashboard.html`, browser-local JSON import and a portable filtered JSON export.
This release does not connect to a live SIEM tenant or deploy an Internet-facing web service.
See the [dashboard guide](docs/DASHBOARDS_ES.md) for data integration, API routes and limits.

**Identity threat analytics: security data engineering, reproducible machine learning, and human-led investigation.**

A portfolio project by Carlo Alessandro Cabrera. AegisLake turns authentication events into a small security data lake, compares detection methods under an analyst workload budget, and produces an offline investigation dashboard.

> Previous release 0.1.2: 49 tests passed with 91% measured coverage; dependency audit, Bicep build and non-root Docker execution passed. [Execution evidence](https://github.com/krlokbrera/aegislake/actions/runs/41222003014). Live Azure deployment remains pending.

[Spanish guide](docs/GUIA_ES.md) · [Research and design](docs/RESEARCH_ES.md) · [Azure](docs/AZURE.md) · [Model card](docs/MODEL_CARD.md) · [Data card](docs/DATA_CARD.md) · [Interview walkthrough](docs/CV_AND_INTERVIEW_ES.md)

## Why this project

A suspicious login is useful only if an analyst can investigate it. This project treats detection as a data product: reliable ingestion, explicit data contracts, temporal evaluation, traceable evidence, and bounded review workload. It combines the data engineering and cybersecurity experience that a generic classification notebook usually separates.

| Capability | Implemented evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Data engineering | Bronze snapshot, validated silver Parquet partitions, SQL feature aggregation, gold outputs |
| Analytics | Daily SOC KPIs, quality reconciliation, feature drift diagnostics, offline report |
| Applied AI | Rules, Isolation Forest, logistic regression, hybrid score, validation-only model selection |
| ML evaluation | Train/validation/test by time; average precision; precision/recall; false positives; daily capacity |
| Security | Keyed pseudonymization, no model pickle loading, private Blob access, no keys in code |
| Human oversight | Evidence summaries and a local append-only-at-application-level review ledger |
| Azure engineering | Bicep, optional finite Container Apps Job, managed identity, scoped RBAC |
| Delivery | Python package and CLI, Docker, tests, GitHub Actions, source-backed design documentation |

## Run the local demo

Python 3.11 or 3.12 is recommended. Run from the repository root:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
# Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# Linux/macOS: source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install ".[dev]"
aegislake demo --output runs
```

The CLI prints the completed run directory. Open its `report.html` in your browser. It is a self-contained, offline dashboard with workload charts, model comparisons, searchable evidence and paginated alerts. Open the linked `mitre.html` page to explore the curated ATT&CK map and jump to alerts filtered by technique. Keep the HTML pages and their `attack-mapping.json` and `dettect-techniques.yaml` downloads together. Alerts expose candidate tactic IDs as well as technique IDs. [DeTT&CT integration and scoring scope](docs/DETTCT_ES.md).

Default workload: 30 days, 50 identities, seed 42, 18 training days, six validation days, six test days, and at most 25 queued user windows per test day. These are simulator settings, not organization-wide capacity recommendations.

```bash
pytest --cov=aegislake --cov-report=term-missing
ruff check src tests scripts
pip-audit --progress-spinner off
```

For Docker:

```bash
docker build -t aegislake:local .
docker run --rm -v aegis-demo:/app/runs aegislake:local
# The named volume retains output; copy it using a separate read-only container if needed.
```

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Synthetic JSONL or canonical labeled export"] --> B["Bronze snapshot and quality checks"]
    B --> C["Silver Parquet by UTC date"]
    B --> Q["Rejected line references"]
    C --> D["Closed 15-minute SQL windows"]
    D --> E["Temporal evaluation and model selection"]
    E --> F["Gold alert queue and offline report"]
    F --> G["Analyst review ledger"]
    F --> H["Private Azure reports"]
```

The reference implementation is single-node batch processing. It does not claim streaming delivery guarantees, distributed exactly-once processing, or incident response automation.

## Useful commands

```bash
# Evaluate your canonical labeled dataset:
aegislake run --input data/labeled-events.jsonl --output runs --train-days 18 --validation-days 6

# Record a review; replace the run path and alert identifier:
aegislake review --run runs/RUN_ID --alert-id ALERT_ID --decision needs_context --reviewer analyst-01

# Adapt an existing Graph JSON export after setting AEGIS_PSEUDONYM_KEY privately:
aegislake adapt-entra --input data/graph-export.json --output data/pseudonymous.jsonl

# Score future unlabeled events from an integrity-checked reference:
aegislake score --reference runs/RUN_ID --input data/future.jsonl --output runs/future-batch

# Upload only synthetic reports after Azure login and scoped RBAC setup:
python -m pip install ".[azure]"
aegislake publish --run runs/RUN_ID --account YOUR_STORAGE_ACCOUNT
```

Synthetic-trained references require an explicit `--allow-domain-shift` for new-batch scoring. This is an experimental interoperability path, not validation on Entra telemetry.

## Outputs

Each completed run contains:

- `bronze/events.jsonl`: original snapshot, kept locally.
- `silver/event_date=.../events.parquet`: validated partitions.
- `quarantine/rejected.json` and `quality.json`: disposition accounting.
- `gold/*_features.parquet`: train, validation and test windows.
- `gold/alerts.json`: evidence queue without ground-truth labels.
- `report.html`, `mitre.html` and `report.json`: investigation dashboard, curated technique explorer, results and limitations.
- `dashboard.html` and `dashboard.json`: linked native charts, portable data snapshot and optional local API exploration.
- `manifest.json`: input hash, configuration, versions and output hashes.
- `reviews.sqlite`: created when an analyst records a decision.

Raw telemetry and outputs are ignored by Git. GitHub Actions uploads only synthetic reports, manifests, coverage and an environment record.

## Verification evidence and remaining scope

Read [VALIDATION_STATUS.md](docs/VALIDATION_STATUS.md) for observed checks and remaining limits. [A generated synthetic report](examples/demo/report.html), its JSON metrics and manifest are included for inspection. Azure student access and live deployment are pending.

## License

MIT for original project code. External datasets retain their own terms and attribution requirements. No employer or client data is included.
docs/DASHBOARDS_ES.md:
# Dashboards nativos dentro de AegisLake

La sección **Dashboards** calcula gráficos interactivos sobre las ventanas de alerta de una ejecución.
Comparte la navegación con Overview y MITRE ATT&CK; no incrusta capturas, iframes, Power BI o Grafana.
No requiere CDN, licencia de BI, API key ni servicios cloud adicionales.

## Abrir la interfaz conectada

```sh
python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'
aegislake demo --seed 7 --output runs
aegislake serve --runs runs --port 8767
```

Abre <http://127.0.0.1:8767/dashboard.html>. El servidor se enlaza exclusivamente a loopback.
Solo expone los informes permitidos y una API de lectura; no publica bronze, silver, Parquet, modelos,
credenciales ni listados del sistema de archivos. No implementa autenticación multiusuario y no debe
exponerse a Internet mediante túneles o proxies. La implantación cloud sigue siendo un trabajo separado.

## Exploración enlazada

- **Actividad temporal:** selecciona una barra para fijar las fechas UTC. Los intervalos extensos
  se agrupan en un máximo de 40 barras; el gráfico indica el tamaño de cada intervalo.
- **Hipótesis ATT&CK:** selecciona una técnica o el grupo sin mapeo curado. Las hipótesis de una misma
  ventana pueden solaparse; sus recuentos no se suman para obtener un total de incidentes.
- **Mapa horario:** selecciona una combinación de día de la semana y hora UTC, agregada entre semanas.
- **Identidades:** selecciona una identidad exacta de las ocho con más ventanas en el filtro actual.
- **Puntuaciones:** selecciona un intervalo de ranking. Los scores no son probabilidades ni severidades.
- Los controles de fecha, búsqueda, técnica y puntuación mínima afectan a todos los gráficos, KPIs
  y a la cola paginada. **Clear filters** elimina también las selecciones hechas en los gráficos.

Los KPIs cuentan ventanas en la cola y entidades distintas, no todas las autenticaciones ni ataques
confirmados. El pico diario pertenece a la selección actual. La precisión y el recall, cuando existen,
se muestran aparte como contexto de la evaluación etiquetada completa y no se recalculan con filtros.

## Datos nuevos y SOC/SIEM

El selector **Batch** cambia entre ejecuciones completas. La interfaz puede consultar cada 30 segundos
el catálogo local y seguir el lote más reciente. Es actualización de lotes, no streaming de eventos.
Puede pausarse y refrescarse manualmente. Si falla la API, conserva los últimos datos cargados y muestra
el estado de error; no genera valores nuevos ni borra la evidencia anterior.

El comando existente `score` genera ahora Overview, MITRE, `dashboard.html`, `dashboard.json` y los
mapeos en el directorio de salida. El archivo `scoring.json` se escribe al final como marcador de
finalización. El explorador ignora directorios `.partial` y lotes sin un marcador de finalización.

```sh
# Utiliza datos autorizados y una referencia entrenada/validada para tu dominio.
aegislake score --reference runs/REFERENCE --input data/future.jsonl --output runs/batch-2026-11-01
aegislake serve --runs runs
```

Las entradas deben cumplir el contrato canónico; para exportaciones locales de Microsoft Graph existe
`adapt-entra`, que seudonimiza identificadores mediante una clave local. Esta entrega no establece una
conexión activa con un tenant, Sentinel, Elastic o Splunk y no extrae telemetría de cuentas reales.
Los lotes sin etiquetas carecen de precisión/recall y la procedencia de su fuente debe revisarse.
El uso de una referencia sintética para datos nuevos continúa requiriendo `--allow-domain-shift`;
ese permiso no valida su eficacia operativa.

## Modo sin servidor e importación

Cada ejecución incluye un `dashboard.html` autónomo con su snapshot embebido. Puede abrirse desde
disco o desde el informe, con el mismo comportamiento de filtros y gráficos. No consulta la API.

**Open dashboard JSON** abre otro `dashboard.json` dentro del navegador. El archivo no se sube al
servidor y la actualización de API queda pausada. **Refresh now** recupera el lote seleccionado de la
API local. La procedencia de un archivo importado es declarada por ese archivo, no certificada.
Se rechazan versiones desconocidas, IDs duplicados, scores inválidos y archivos de más de 20 MiB
o 20 000 alertas. El contenido se inserta como texto y no como HTML ejecutable.

**Export selection** prepara una descarga y un panel con el JSON copiable de las filas que cumplen los filtros, sin limitarse a la página
de la cola. Incluye los criterios de selección y omite métricas globales de eficacia para que no se
confundan con resultados medidos sobre ese subconjunto. Puede volver a importarse.

## API y límites

| Ruta | Resultado |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/runs` | Catálogo de lotes completos y claves opacas; sin rutas del equipo |
| `GET /api/runs/{key}/dashboard` | Snapshot versionado `aegislake.dashboard.v1` |
| `GET /report.html?run={key}` | Overview del lote seleccionado |
| `GET /mitre.html?run={key}` | Mapa y mapeos del mismo lote |

Las respuestas usan `no-store`; no se habilita CORS. Se rechazan Host y Origin ajenos al servidor
local. Los identificadores de API no se convierten en rutas arbitrarias. Esto limita el alcance del
explorador local; no sustituye un backend autenticado apto para producción.

La versión 0.2.0 cambia el identificador de las nuevas evaluaciones. Regenera las referencias con esa
versión; el control de integridad sigue rechazando referencias creadas con otra versión del código.

Fuentes de diseño y límites:
[Python HTTP server](https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html),
[Microsoft Sentinel Workbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/monitor-your-data) y
[Azure Monitor: informes interactivos](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/visualize/workbooks-interactive-reports).
Los Workbooks son una alternativa dentro de Azure; no se presentan aquí como una integración desplegada.

# Verificación del frontend

## Dashboards 0.2.0

La nueva sección Dashboards utiliza las filas de `dashboard.json` tanto en HTML autónomo como en la
interfaz conectada a la API local. La revisión de navegador comprobó filtros enlazados por técnica
y fecha, selección de día/hora UTC, bins de puntuación, paginación, búsquedas vacías, conservación
de filtros al refrescar y selección exacta de identidad desde el gráfico.

Se probó además la detección de un lote nuevo de scoring: la API lo incorporó sin reiniciar y
la interfaz mostró sus 23 alertas sin precisión o recall. Los datos de esa prueba son una continuación
sintética, no telemetría de un SOC real. La importación válida se procesó dentro del navegador con la
actualización de API pausada; cinco entradas inválidas se rechazaron mediante el validador JavaScript.

La suite local completa pasa 61 pruebas con 90 % de cobertura Python. Incluye peticiones HTTP reales,
aislamiento de rutas y orígenes, descubrimiento de nuevos lotes y regresión del pipeline de scoring.
El panel copiable de exportación se comprobó en navegador: al filtrar T1078 produce cinco filas,
todas con esa hipótesis y sin métricas globales heredadas. La navegación MITRE → cola conserva
la clave del lote y el filtro de técnica. El gestor de descargas del navegador y el diseño móvil de esta
nueva sección no se dan por verificados. Las comprobaciones móviles descritas abajo corresponden
a Overview/MITRE de la entrega anterior. Consulta [la guía de dashboards](DASHBOARDS_ES.md).

## Overview y MITRE de la entrega anterior

El informe offline utiliza dos páginas: `report.html` para métricas e investigación y `mitre.html`
para técnicas, tácticas candidatas y el traspaso de evaluación a DeTT&CT. Los archivos descargables
`attack-mapping.json` y `dettect-techniques.yaml` deben conservarse junto a las páginas.

## Comportamiento comprobado en navegador

- Búsqueda por identidad: la muestra seed-7 devuelve cuatro ventanas para employee-0043.
- Búsqueda sin coincidencias: estado vacío y paginación desactivada.
- Paginación: ocho alertas por página, con segunda página 9–16 de 146.
- Filtro T1078: cinco ventanas, todas con esa hipótesis.
- Orden temporal descendente y evidencias desplegables.
- Selección de técnica en MITRE y navegación a la cola filtrada correspondiente.
- Marco móvil de 390 px: ambas páginas sin desbordamiento horizontal del documento.
- Contenido y estilos integrados sin CDN, fuentes externas, analítica o peticiones de datos.

Las pruebas unitarias comprueban escape de HTML, preservación de métricas, recuentos por ventana,
estados vacíos, conservación de técnicas desconocidas y estructura del YAML. La integración
comprueba manifiestos y la publicación de todos los archivos enlazados antes del marcador cloud.

La muestra publicada se regenera con puntuaciones completas; no depende de la extracción de tarjetas
HTML utilizada para la primera revisión local. Los resultados describen datos sintéticos.

Consulta [el registro de ejecución](VALIDATION_STATUS.md) para los resultados medidos de CI y
[la guía DeTT&CT](DETTCT_ES.md) para el significado de las exportaciones y puntuaciones iniciales.
